messages.subject: Rescale in writeWave not working
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I have a curious problem  and I am sure this has worked before, but I can't figure it out.

I am downmixing/sampling a 44k stereo file to 22k mono and want to export it after, but I don't want to normalise it.

Jerome had recommended me the rescale trick - just rescale it by its old range. However I am getting

Error in writeWave(resampled, soundfile, rescale = range(resampled@left)) :
  unused argument (rescale = range(resampled@left))

Code is below and file is attached! Any pointers?

Simon
------------------------------------------
    soundfile<-("test_rs01_20080430_143000.wav")
    full<-readWave(soundfile)
    mix<-0.5*full@left+0.5*full@right
    resampled<-resamp(mix,f=detectsamplerate$sample.rate,g=22050, output="Wave")
    writeWave(resampled, soundfile, rescale=range(resampled@left))

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Rescale in writeWave not working
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,
The argument 'rescale' is for the function savewav() of seewave, not for writeWave() of tuneR.
So try:
savewav(resampled, f=22050, filename=soundfile, rescale=range(resampled@left)
HTH
Jerome

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Rescale in writeWave not working
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Ben is right, you are not normalizing. But yes it is either save wav with the 'rescale' argument or writeWave without anything else. Here is a working example with both (except save wav apparently centers max and min around 0, so I'd recommend writeWav):

------------------------
library(seewave)
library(tuneR)

data(tico)
range(tico@left)

tico.resamp <- resamp(tico, f=ti...@samp.rate,g=11025, output="Wave")

range(tico.resamp@left)

writeWave(tico.resamp, filename = 'tico-resamp.wav')

tico.read <- readWave('tico-resamp.wav')
range(tico.read@left)

savewav(tico.resamp, filename = 'tico-resamp-save.wav', rescale=range(tico.resamp@left))
tico.read2 <- readWave('tico-resamp-save.wav')
range(tico.read2@left)
------------------------------------------

Cheers,
Camille

messages.subject: Acquire amplitude values for given time and frequency coordinates
messages.subject_clean: Acquire amplitude values for given time and frequency coordinates
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I'm working on some analysis in which I wish to acquire amplitude values for a grid of time and amplitude coordinates. The simplest way to do this would be to store the result of 'spectro' as an object and use the $time and $frequency to acquire $amp values. However, this approach is linked to the window length (FFT = wl = 512) and it generates a very large amount of data.

> som1 <- readWave("olfersii.wav")
>
> sonogram1 <- spectro(som1, wl=512, tlim=c(0,4), flim=c(0,15), plot=F)
>
> length(sonogram1$time)
[1] 344
> length(sonogram1$freq)
[1] 175
> length(sonogram1$amp)
[1] 60200

What I was hoping to do would be to simplify the grid of coordinates without the need to change FFT values (which would incur in spectrogram changes).
By using the current window length, the grid of coordinates looks like this (fig 'original grid.jpeg' attached):

plot(x= c(0, 4), y=c(0,15))
abline(v=sonogram1$time, h=sonogram1$freq)

Whereas I would like the grid to be like this (fig 'intended grid.jpeg' attached):

plot(x= c(0, 4), y=c(0,15))
abline(v=seq(0, 4, length.out = 100))
abline(h=seq(0, 15, length.out = 80))

In which I would acquire a amplitude value for each set of time and frequency coordinates in the grid.

I gave a look in seewave documentation and searched for similar approaches, but I couldn't sort a way of doing it.

I'll appreciate any help.

Pedro

messages.subject: ffilter small frequency ranges
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm using the function ffilter from seewave to filter out small frequency bands (10 Hz or 100Hz) from a sound signal (44.1kHz, 16bit) and I observed that for frequency bands smaller than 150Hz, there is a particular pattern that appears in the frequency spectrum that I can't explain. Sistematically, each x frequency bands, there is one band with lower amplitude than the rest and then the amplitude of the next band rises again (see figure 1). I appears as two signals instead of one. It does not happens when the frequency bands are bigger than 150Hz. You can see both spectrums in the files attached. Does anybody knows what is caussing this pattern?

I let you here the code I used to produce the figures:

a <- readWave(file=file.choose(),header=FALSE)

Figure 1:
ffa <- ffilter(a, from = 1000, to = 1050, bandpass = TRUE, wl=512, ovlp=50,  output="Wave")
b <- spectro(ffa,wl=512, ovlp=50, plot = FALSE, norm=FALSE)
amplitude <- apply(b$amp, 1, mean)
plot(b$freq,amplitude)

Figure 2:
ffa <- ffilter(a, from = 1000, to = 2000, bandpass = TRUE, wl=512, ovlp=50,  output="Wave")
b <- spectro(ffa,wl=512, ovlp=50, plot = FALSE, norm=FALSE)
amplitude <- apply(b$amp, 1, mean)
plot(b$freq,amplitude)

Thank you very much for your help
Best wishes

messages.subject: Re: Small error in spec function (and proposed fix)
messages.subject_clean: Small error in spec function (and proposed fix)
messages.body_plain:
I confirmed there is a problem. The attached example is the result of 2000 mathematically generated damped sine waves. Analysis is over a 2 second period at 44.1 kHz sampling rate - which means an odd number of points. Frequency accuracy error is biased by half an fft bin at the top end - and this is the result of an error in how the x vector is calculated within spec.

Script along these lines works

        x = seq(0, (f/2), length.out = length(y) + 1)/1000
        x = head(x, n = length(x)-1)

where y is the vector of of FFT amplitudes, already cut in half from what comes out of fft()

Dan

On Tuesday, 21 November 2017 00:01:03 UTC, Dan Ridley-Ellis wrote:
>
> Hi
> I've been throwing a bunch of mathematically generated waves at the spec function and I've noticed that it makes a small error when the wave has an odd number of points in the time domain.   I think this caused by the way that the vector of frequency bins is calculated in the spec function.
>
>
> The error means that frequencies at the high end are, on average, in error by half the width of a fft frequency bin when there an odd number of points in the time domain.
>
> If there an even number of points, no problems
>
>
>
> In the spec function there is the code for the frequency bins x:
>
>
>  if (is.null(at)) {
>
>           x <- seq(0, (f/2) - (f/n), length.out = n%/%2)/1000
>
>         }
>
>         else {
>
>           x <- seq(0, (f/2) - (f/wl), length.out = n%/%2)/1000
>
>         }
>
>
>
> This seems to work better (but I am not sure why)
>
>
>   if (is.null(at)) {
>
>           x <- seq(0, (f/2) - (f/n) - n%%2, length.out = n%/%2)/1000
>
>         }
>
>         else {
>
>           x <- seq(0, (f/2) - (f/wl) - n%%2, length.out = n%/%2)/1000
>
>         }
>
>
>
> Dan
